newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends down on China rumor, soyoil up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends down on China rumor, soyoil up.

text.p: CBOT soymeal ended lower on Tuesday amid talk China had purchased South American supplies, while soyoil closed higher on fund soyoil/soymeal spreading, traders said.

Floor sources cited talk China bought two to three cargoes of South American soymeal. Exporters could not confirm the rumors but traders said it suggested demand for U.S. soymeal was weakening as Argentina and Brazil continued to ship.
Soyoil drew strength from active soyoil/soymeal spreading which lent support to soyoil. Trade sources said funds sold at least 900 lots soymeal and bought 1,500 lots soyoil.
Chartists said technical outlooks for soymeal were bearish and some floor sources said traders were eager to dump soymeal futures and buy soyoil.
Traders noted soymeal raced to 8-1/2-year highs this spring on supply concerns while soyoil struggled. They said soymeal may have peaked while soyoil remained more competitive.
Soymeal ended $3.70 per ton lower to unchanged with May down $0.70 at $275.00. Soyoil closed 0.28 to 0.08 cent per lb higher with May up 0.28 at 24.18.
Soymeal recovered strength late on floor speculation that a strike at Brazil's Santos port would spread to a national level this week, jeopardizing soymeal exports from Brazil's Paranagua port.
Paranagua exports more soymeal than Santos.
"The head of the port in Paranagua went to Santos for a meeting so if it escalates it could stop exports," a floor source said.

Stevedores at Brazil's Santos port are on strike and the stoppage is preventing three vessels waiting to unload wheat and load soybeans from docking at public terminals. Union officials were deciding whether to call a national strike.
On the day, R.J. O'Brien sold 300 lots May soymeal, Prudential Securities sold 200 May and Smith Barney sold 200 August, pit sources said.
Griffin Trading bought 600 lots July soyoil, Smith Barney bought 300 July, 100 May and 100 August and Dean Witter bought 300 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 20,000 lots, compared with Monday's actual volume of 20,841 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 17,000 lots, above Monday's 14,233.
